# Manifest { #labdata.manifest.Manifest }

```python
labdata.manifest.Manifest(directory, files, stamps=dict())
```

What one directory of a repository publishes.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

<code>[**directory**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative directory the manifest governs, ``""`` at the root of the repository.

<code>[**files**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[str](`str`), [str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Keys in the order they were written, each mapped to its description. A key is a path relative to `directory`, a bare file name, a glob pattern over either, or -- written with a leading ``/`` -- a path or pattern from the root of the repository, naming a file outside `directory`.

<code>[**stamps**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Stamp](`labdata.manifest.Stamp`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The content stamps, under the same keys as `files` and only for the keys that carry one. A key with a stamp names a link: a symbolic link whose target holds the real content. Empty for a manifest that publishes no links.

### anchored_prefixes { #labdata.manifest.Manifest.anchored_prefixes }

```python
labdata.manifest.Manifest.anchored_prefixes()
```

Where to look for the files this manifest names from the repository root.

A key written from the root may name a file anywhere in the repository,
so finding what it names means listing more than the results directory.
Each such key contributes the literal part of its path, up to its first
glob character, which is the least that has to be listed.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[List](`typing.List`)\[[str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative paths to list, without duplicates and without any that lies inside another. ``""`` stands for the whole repository. Empty when the manifest names nothing outside `directory`.

#### See Also {.doc-section .doc-section-see-also}

[](`labdata.manifest.Manifest.describe`)

### describe { #labdata.manifest.Manifest.describe }

```python
labdata.manifest.Manifest.describe(path)
```

Look up what a file is, and thereby whether it is published at all.

An exact key wins over a glob, and a full path wins over a bare file
name, so a specific description can be given for one file among many
covered by a pattern. A key written from the repository root is the most
specific spelling of all and is tried first. Globs are tried in the
order they were written.

A key that does not start with ``/`` only ever reaches inside
`directory`: a bare file name is matched against files this manifest
governs, never against the same name elsewhere in the repository.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**path**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative path of the file.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The description, ``""`` when the file is published with none, or `None` when it is not published.

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
m = parse('files:\n  "*.csv": a table\n  hits.csv: the good one\n', "results")
m.describe("results/hits.csv")
# 'the good one'
```

### stamp { #labdata.manifest.Manifest.stamp }

```python
labdata.manifest.Manifest.stamp(path)
```

Look up the content a file's link stands for.

Keys are matched as [](`labdata.manifest.Manifest.describe`) matches
them, except that no glob is tried: a stamp identifies one file's
content, so [](`labdata.manifest.parse`) refuses to put one on a
pattern.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**path**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative path of the file.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[Stamp](`labdata.manifest.Stamp`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The stamp, or `None` when the file is not published as a link. A file with no stamp is an ordinary committed file, versioned by git itself.

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
m = parse('files:\n  big.csv:\n    size: 12\n    sha256: "%s"\n' % ("a" * 64), "results")
m.stamp("results/big.csv")
# Stamp(sha256='aaaa...', size=12)
```
